connectors.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in the app container. See the documentation https://docs.camunda.io/docs/self-managed/components/connectors/connectors-configuration/ for more details.

console.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in the app container. See the documentation https://docs.camunda.io/docs/self-managed/components/console/configuration/ for more details.

global.documentStore.type.aws.accessKeyI.description: can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the access key ID.
defines the key within the existing secret object.
can be used to provide the access key ID as a plain-text value for non-production usage.

global.documentStore.type.aws.bucket.description: Name of the AWS S3 bucket.

global.documentStore.type.aws.bucketPath.description: can be used to define a key prefix within the S3 bucket (for example documents/invoices), not an endpoint URL.

global.documentStore.type.aws.irsa.enabl.description: if true, no static AWS credentials are injected into pods, so the AWS SDK resolves credentials through its default provider chain; this supports both IRSA and EKS Pod Identity. If false (default), credentials are required via existingSecret or accessKeyId/secretAccessKey configuration.

global.documentStore.type.aws.region.description: AWS region for the S3 bucket. (example: us-east-1)

global.documentStore.type.aws.secretAcce.description: can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the secret access key.
defines the key within the existing secret object.
can be used to provide the secret access key as a plain-text value for non-production usage.

global.documentStore.type.gcp.secret.exi.description: can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the service account JSON.
defines the key within the existing secret object.

global.ingress.className.description: Ingress.className defines the class or configuration of ingress which should be used by the controller

global.ingress.enabled.description: if true, an ingress resource is deployed. Only useful if an ingress controller is available, like Ingress-NGINX.

global.ingress.host.description: (DEPRECATED - use global.host instead) If not specified the rules applies to all inbound http traffic, if specified the rule applies to that host. Supports templating (e.g., {{ .Release.Name }}.example.com).

global.ingress.tls.enabled.description: if true, then tls is configured on the ingress resource. If enabled the Ingress.host need to be defined.

global.ingress.tls.secretName.description: defines the secret name which contains the TLS private key and certificate

global.license.secret.existingSecret.description: can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the license.

global.license.secret.inlineSecret.description: can be used to provide the license as a plain-text value for non-production usage.

global.security.authentication.method.description: defines the authentication method which should be used. Possible values: basic, oidc. Could be overridden in each component.

key within the secret that holds the PEM-encoded CA bundle.

identity.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in the app container. See the documentation https://docs.camunda.io/docs/self-managed/components/management-identity/miscellaneous/configuration-variables/ for more details.

identity.externalDatabase.secret.existin.description: can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the password.
defines the key within the existing secret object.

identity.externalDatabase.secret.inlineS.description: can be used to provide the password as a plain-text value for non-production usage.

operate.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in each Operate container

optimize.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in the app container. See the documentation https://docs.camunda.io/docs/self-managed/components/optimize/configuration/system-configuration/ for more details.

orchestration.clusterSize.description: defines the amount of brokers (=replicas), which are deployed via helm

orchestration.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in the app container. See the documentation https://docs.camunda.io/docs/self-managed/components/orchestration-cluster/core-settings/configuration/properties/ for more details.

orchestration.ingress.grpc.className.description: defines the class or configuration of ingress which should be used by the controller

orchestration.ingress.grpc.enabled.description: if true, an ingress resource is deployed with the Zeebe gateway deployment. Only useful if an ingress controller is available, like nginx.

orchestration.ingress.grpc.host.description: can be used to define the host of the ingress rule. https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/#ingress-rules

orchestration.ingress.grpc.tls.enabled.description: if true, then tls is configured on the ingress resource. If enabled the Ingress.host need to be defined.

orchestration.ingress.grpc.tls.secretNam.description: defines the secret name which contains the TLS private key and certificate

orchestration.partitionCount.description: defines how many partitions are set up in the cluster

orchestration.pvcSize.description: defines the persistent volume claim size, which is used by each broker pod https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#persistentvolumeclaims

orchestration.pvcStorageClassName.description: can be used to set the storage class name which should be used by the persistent volume claim.

orchestration.replicationFactor.description: defines how each partition is replicated, the value defines the number of nodes

orchestration.security.authentication.oi.description: defines the audience, which is used by Orchestration Cluster.
defines the client id, which is used by Orchestration Cluster in authentication flows.
can be used to set group claim.
defines the root (or redirect) URL, which is used by Keycloak to access Tasklist.
can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the client secret.
defines the key within the existing secret object.
can be used to provide the client secret as a plain-text value for non-production usage.
can be used to set username claim.

tasklist.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables on each Tasklist container

webModeler.restapi.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in the app container. See the documentation https://docs.camunda.io/docs/self-managed/components/modeler/web-modeler/configuration/ for more details.

webModeler.restapi.externalDatabase.data.description: The database name (used when url is not provided)

webModeler.restapi.externalDatabase.host.description: Database host (used when url is not provided)

webModeler.restapi.externalDatabase.port.description: Database port number (used when url is not provided)

webModeler.restapi.externalDatabase.secr.description: can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the password.
defines the key within the existing secret object.
can be used to provide the password as a plain-text value for non-production usage.

webModeler.restapi.externalDatabase.user.description: (DEPRECATED - use webModeler.restapi.externalDatabase.username instead) defines the database user

webModeler.restapi.mail.fromAddress.description: defines the email address that will be displayed as the sender of emails sent by WebModeler

webModeler.restapi.mail.fromName.description: defines the name that will be displayed as the sender of emails sent by WebModeler

webModeler.restapi.mail.secret.existingS.description: can be used to reference an existing Kubernetes Secret containing the SMTP password.
defines the key within the existing secret object.

webModeler.restapi.mail.secret.inlineSec.description: can be used to provide the SMTP password as a plain-text value for non-production usage.

webModeler.restapi.mail.smtpHost.description: defines the host name of the SMTP server to be used by WebModeler

webModeler.restapi.mail.smtpPort.description: defines the port number of the SMTP server

webModeler.restapi.mail.smtpTlsEnabled.description: if true, enforces TLS encryption for SMTP connections (using STARTTLS)

webModeler.restapi.mail.smtpUser.description: can be used to provide a user for the SMTP server

webModeler.websockets.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in the app container. See the documentation https://docs.camunda.io/docs/self-managed/components/modeler/web-modeler/configuration/#configuration-of-the-websocket-component for more details.

zeebe.env.description: can be used to set extra environment variables in each zeebe broker container
